union.summary: Re-implemented `asciiTrim` uses a backtracking anchored-whitespace regex (`[\s]+$`) on attacker-controlled note text — quadratic ReDoS that can freeze the renderer thread
union.evidence: The new lheading rule replaces upstream's native `.trim()` with `str.replace(/^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g, '')` (lines 19-23), applied at line 128 to `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false)` — i.e. raw, unbounded, user-authored markdown. The `[ws]+$` alternative is the classic quadratic-trim pattern: for a whitespace run that is NOT at end-of-string, the engine matches the run greedily, fails `$`, backtracks the whole run, then retries from every subsequent index → O(n^2). Attack: a collaborator types/pastes into a shared Yorkie note `a` + ~100k spaces + `b` on one line followed by `===` (or `---`), which routes into this exact code path (setext heading found ⇒ asciiTrim on the whole paragraph). Rendering the note in any viewer's browser burns ~10^9-10^10 regex steps on the main thread, hanging the tab (preview is rendered synchronously on every doc update). Upstream markdown-it deliberately avoids this by using the native trim; the re-creation is what introduces the vector. I did not execute the payload (packages/notes is not present in this checkout), hence medium confidence on the exact wall-clock cost.

union.summary: Vendored fork of markdown-it's `lheading` plus reliance on the private `__rules__` registry silently opts the notes preview out of upstream parser security fixes
union.evidence: `getRuleFn` (lines 204-212) reads `md.block.ruler.__rules__`, an undocumented private field, to recover the stock `list` fn, and `lheadingRule` (lines 78-153) is a hand-copied duplicate of markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs`. markdown-it has shipped hardening/DoS fixes inside individual block rules before; any future patch to `lheading` is dead code here because `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` (line 174) unconditionally overwrites it, and a minor-version refactor of `__rules__` makes `getRuleFn` throw at module init (breaking preview rendering) or, if the shape merely changes, silently changes which fn is delegated to. This is a supply-chain/patch-application weakness rather than a live exploit: pinned-fork drift in a parser that sits directly on untrusted input.

union.summary: Wrapped `list` rule returns `true` in silent mode without running the stock rule's indent/code-block/listIndent guards, widening paragraph-interruption and block-nesting amplification on untrusted input
union.evidence: `wrappedList` (lines 180-192) short-circuits to `return true` whenever `silent && parentType === 'paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(...)`. `isEmptyBulletLine` (lines 31-49) only checks `sCount[line] >= blkIndent` and the marker shape; it skips the stock list rule's `sCount - blkIndent >= 4` (indented-code) and `listIndent >= 0 && sCount - listIndent >= 4` guards. Attacker-supplied input of the form `a` followed by successively-indented lone bullets now terminates paragraphs and opens a new nested list at each line where upstream would refuse, so a small document can drive block-nesting/re-tokenization much deeper than before; markdown-it's `maxNesting` (default 100) is the only remaining cap and preview.ts's options in the diff do not show it being set explicitly. I traced the missing guards by comparison with markdown-it 14 `rules_block/list.mjs` but could not measure an actual parse-time blowup or confirm a case where the non-silent pass also declines (which would surface as markdown-it's 'none of the rules matched' throw, i.e. a render-breaking exception), hence low confidence.

union.summary: Hand-rolled `asciiTrim` regex has quadratic backtracking on attacker-controlled note text (client-side ReDoS), replacing markdown-it's native trim
union.evidence: The vendored lheading copy trims heading content with `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09-\x0d\x20]+|[\x09-\x0d\x20]+$/g` (line 21-22) applied via `str.replace` (line 24) to `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, ...)` — i.e. to raw document text. The second alternative `[ws]+$` is unanchored at the start, so on a setext-heading paragraph containing a long internal whitespace run followed by a non-whitespace char (e.g. `"x" + " ".repeat(200000) + "y\n==="`), the engine retries the greedy class at every whitespace offset and backtracks to the end each time → O(n^2) work with no match. Because notes content is rendered in the browser preview and notes are collaborative (Yorkie-backed), a co-editor can paste such a line and freeze other viewers' tab (availability DoS on untrusted input). Upstream markdown-it uses a native trim here, so this is a regression introduced by re-implementing the rule. Confidence is low because I could not run the timing test — the repository working tree was not reachable from my sandbox (only the tooling/scripts directory was visible), so I reasoned from the diff text alone.

union.summary: Plugin reads markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry and throws at wiring time if absent, turning a dependency bump into a hard render/bundle failure
union.evidence: `getRuleFn` casts `md.block.ruler` to expose `__rules__` and does `throw new Error('markdown-it block rule not found: list')` when the private field/entry is missing. `listEmptyBulletPlugin` is applied at module scope in `preview.ts` (`md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)`), so any markdown-it internal rename makes the notes preview module throw on import rather than degrade — an availability failure of the whole preview surface, not just the #517 behaviour. Not attacker-triggerable, so nit; flagged only because it lives on the input-parsing path.

union.summary: No verified bound/guard review of the new paragraph-terminator shortcut against markdown-it's tokenizer invariants; I could not open the working tree to enumerate the other rules that consume `list` in silent mode
union.evidence: `wrappedList` returns `true` in silent mode (paragraph-terminator mode) for any empty bullet line when `state.parentType === 'paragraph'`, without delegating to the stock rule. `list` is registered in the `alt` chains `['paragraph','reference','blockquote']`, so `blockquote` (lazy-continuation checks) and `reference` also invoke it silently; the `parentType === 'paragraph'` guard looks like it confines the deviation, and a paragraph nested inside a blockquote/list still reaches it. If any caller relies on silent `list` truth implying the non-silent rule will consume the line, markdown-it can end up re-dispatching the line (`paragraph` fallback) or, in the worst case, hitting its internal "block rule didn't increment state.line" / "none of the block rules matched" throw during render of untrusted note text (parser-level DoS). I could not confirm or refute this: the repository files (packages/notes/src/view/*, node_modules/markdown-it/lib/rules_block/*) were not accessible from my sandbox, so no call-site enumeration or exception-handling check of `NotePreview.render` was possible. Reported at low confidence so a verifier with tree access can close it out.
